entries.description: The stranger names Grey Harbor as where Mira lives. Whether Grey Harbor is real, and why Mira cannot return, is left open for chapter 3+.
entries.payoff: Aren finds Grey Harbor on a pre-Blackout chart in the archive — the name is real on paper, though the settlement's present state stays unconfirmed; why Mira cannot return passes to fs-whymira.

entries.description: The sealed note the stranger carries. Planted as a mystery (whose handwriting?), resolved when Aren recognizes Mira's hand in chapter 2.
entries.payoff: Aren opens the note and recognizes Mira's handwriting, overturning his belief that she is dead.

entries.description: Aren's father's pocket watch, stopped at 3:07 — the moment of the Blackout. Aren believes it is simply broken; the stranger will later reveal it marks the exact second the old world ended.
entries.payoff: Corra reveals the watch stopped at 3:07 — the exact second the old world ended; Mira has kept time by tides and shadows since.

entries.description: Mira tried three times to return and the boats came back without her; she sent Corra instead. Neither Corra nor Aren knows why she cannot come herself. Her changed way of keeping time hints she knows something about the Blackout. Open for chapter 4+.

The winter storms will seal the island — twelve days, maybe eleven, when Corra arrives; tightened to nine or ten in chapter 3. The countdown drives Aren's departure decision; open until the departure is resolved.
